newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair-too early to talk of no-confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair-too early to talk of no-confidence vote.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour leader Tony Blair said on Friday it was too early to talk of a no-confidence motion in the government over its refusal to allow a full parliamentary debate on Europe.
He told reporters during a visit to a London primary school: "It is too early to talk about things like that."
"We are going to find any way we can to make the government face up to its responsibilities," Blair said.
A row has erupted over whether three working documents related to the European Union's plans for a single currency should be examined on the floor of the House of Commons.
Eurosceptic members of the ruling Conservative party have joined with Labour in demanding a full-scale debate on Europe.

Major, with a majority of just one in the 651-seat lower chamber, is anxious to avoid a full-scale debate that would doubtless reopen deep divisions over Europe that have dogged his six years as prime minister. Opposition parties believe Major would lose any vote on whether a full debate should be held. A vote of no confidence could follow any such defeat.
